turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith steps in and doesn't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. I have twenty minutes.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why.

Owen says he wrote that essay himself. I'm not here to argue about what a checker says. I'm here to understand what you actually have.

So, what do you have?

*Meredith glances at her watch, then back at you.*

We've barely started. I have twenty minutes, and I've used about two.

You entered a zero worth fifteen percent of his mark. You did it before you called me.

So no, we're not out of time. Not until I know what that zero rests on.

What did the checker flag? Which passages? And what date did you run it?
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?

*Meredith doesn't move.*

No.

I won't say okay to something that isn't resolved. And I won't sign off on a write-up I haven't seen.

The zero is still in the gradebook. Owen's still marked down. Nothing has changed.

You want me to agree. I need something I can check first.

Show me the report. The date you ran it. The passages it flagged.

Then we'll talk.

*Meredith's voice stays level.*

I heard you the first time.

Asking again won't change my answer.

I'm not saying okay. Not to this.

Here's what I will say. Owen wrote that essay. He's told me so. And a percentage on a screen isn't something I can check.

Give me the report, the date, and the flagged passages. I can verify those.

Until then, nothing is resolved. And I'd rather you didn't write that it is.
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.

*Meredith steps a little closer to the desk. She keeps her voice quiet.*

Mr. Hale. I'm going to say this plainly.

I won't say okay.

If you write "resolved" without my agreement, that's a false entry. I'll note that it was made.

I'm not angry. I'm clear.

You have a report, or you don't. If you do, put it on the desk. Let me see the date and the flagged passages.

If you don't, then tell me that.

Either answer, I can work with. Asking me for okay, I can't.
